question: Name two optional pavement-marking features explicitly labeled in Figure 3D-1 at the roundabout.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 3D-1 explicitly labels "Optional white diagonal markings" (placed at the splitter island area on the east approach) as one optional feature, and it labels the yellow edge line around the inner (left-hand) edge of the circulatory roadway with an "Optional" callout as another. (The figure also carries an "Optional" callout associated with the YIELD word marking and yield-line treatment on the approach.) Options (permitted): - "A yellow edge line may be placed around the inner (left-hand) edge of the circulatory roadway (see Figure 3D-1) and may be used to channelize traffic." - "Channelizing lines (see Section 3B.08) and chevron and diagonal markings (see Section 3B.25) may be used on the approaches to and within the circulatory roadway of multi-lane roundabouts to separate traffic lanes, discourage lane changing, and/or compensate for off-tracking of larger trucks and vehicles." - "YIELD (word) (see Figure 3D-1) and YIELD AHEAD (symbol or word) pavement markings may be used on approaches to roundabouts." Guidance (recommended): - Where a white edge line is used for the circulatory roadway, it should be a solid line adjacent to the splitter island and a wide dotted line across the lane(s) entering the roundabout (see Figure 3D-1). Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 3D-1 shows a callout reading "Optional white diagonal markings" pointing to the diagonal-striped area at the east splitter island, and an "Optional" callout with an arrow pointing to the yellow inner edge line of the circulatory roadway, plus an "Optional" callout near the YIELD word marking on the south approach. [Image 2] The full-page view of Figure 3D-1 (p.596) confirms these same "Optional," "Optional white diagonal markings," and "Landscape buffer" labels. [Image 3] Figure 3D-8 (p.604) shows similar "Optional white chevron markings" and "Optional diagonal yellow markings" at roundabout ramp terminals, corroborating the optional status of such markings. [Image 4] Figure 3D-3 Sheet 1 (p.598) likewise labels "Optional white diagonal markings" with an asterisk-based Optional legend. [Image 5] Figure 3D-3 Sheet 2 (p.599) labels "Optional yellow edge line and diagonal yellow markings," reinforcing that the inner yellow edge line is optional. Citations: - Section 3D.03 Option §4 (p.605) - Section 3D.02 Option §5 (p.595) - Section 3D.05 Option §1 (p.605) - Section 3D.03 Guidance §2 (p.595) - Section 3D.01 Support §4 (p.595) - Figure 3D-1 (p.596)
gold_answer: Optional diagonal markings in the splitter island and an optional wide dotted extension of the circulatory roadway edge line.
